title: degradation-detector-and-soft-priority-throttle-for-continual-batching
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Add degradation detector and soft-priority throttling to continuous batcher to reduce starvation and tail latency; opt-in via runtime flag
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to see rare but impactful tail-latency episodes in the continuous batcher when a small subset of long-lived KV-heavy requests either pin slots or push lower-priority traffic into starvation. Previous mitigations (slot decay, jittered timeouts) reduced frequency but didn't prevent multi-minute degradations on degraded bursty workloads.

This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) a lightweight degradation detector that watches queue aging and worklet progress at multiple percentiles and flags emergent starvation patterns, and (2) a soft-priority throttle that temporarily reduces admission or offers graceful backpressure to low-importance routes when the detector is tripped. Both are tuned to avoid hard rejects and to be reversible without operator involvement.

Design summary:
- Degradation detector: computes moving-window percentiles (50/95/99) of queue wait time and per-slot progress metrics. It uses an exponential smoothing window and a hysteresis counter to avoid flapping. When (a) 95th percentile wait exceeds P95_THRESHOLD *and* (b) per-slot progress falls below a configured fraction for N consecutive windows, detector enters ALERT state.
- Soft-priority throttle: when ALERT state is active, the admission controller applies a probabilistic throttle to requests tagged with priority <= SOFT_PRIORITY (default: background). The throttle reduces accepted admission rate by up to SOFT_THROTTLE_MAX (default 60%) but still queues a bounded fraction to ensure forward progress.
- Timeouts and requeue behavior: the change adds a bounded exponential backoff to immediate requeue attempts so that transient failures don't amplify queue spikes. A short randomized jitter prevents synchronization artifacts.
- KV-cache interaction: long-running KV-heavy requests are given a temporary 'KV-guard' lease extension to avoid losing warm cache references on repeated preemption; the detector also watches for elevated cache-eviction rates and will avoid aggressive throttle if cache-eviction spikes would cause worse thrash.

Implementation notes:
- All logic is implemented in runner/scheduler/continuous_batcher.* with a small shim in runner/scheduler/admission_controller.go to evaluate priority tags.
- Config knobs are exposed via runtime flags and feature-gate (continuous.batch.degradation_detector, continuous.batch.soft_throttle). Defaults are OFF for old clusters; on new clusters the feature is enabled by default.
- Unit tests cover detector state transitions, throttling probability math, and requeue jitter. Integration tests simulate KV-heavy and spike workloads and assert no increase in median latency and a reduction in 95/99 tails.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector core + state machine implemented
- [x] Probabilistic throttle policy implemented
- [x] KV-guard lease and cache-safety checks
- [x] Runtime flags + feature gate + docs stub
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Benchmarked on perf-lab with representative workloads

Microbenchmarks (perf-lab, c6g large, 2h runs):
- Baseline (no patch): P50=12ms, P95=210ms, P99=980ms, incidents: 4/2h
- With patch enabled (default tuning): P50=12ms, P95=140ms (-33%), P99=420ms (-57%), incidents: 0/2h
- Worst-case background-heavy workload: admitted throughput reduced 27% but overall tail reduced and SLA for foreground routes preserved

Safety & rollout:
- Feature gated and off-by-default for clusters older than v2025-10 image
- Default tuning favors permissive behavior to avoid false positives
- Operator escalation: metrics (continuous.batch.detector_state, continuous.batch.throttle_effective_rate) added to console dashboard
- Rollback: feature gate flip + pod restart suffices for rollback

Commits summary:
- 7 commits, squashed on merge. High level: add detector state machine and tests; admission controller throttle; KV-guard lease; requeue/backoff jitter; runtime flags and docs.

Code snippets (illustrative):
- detector transition: if p95_wait > config.P95Threshold && progress_ratio < config.MinProgress then state = ALERT
- throttle acceptance: accept_with_prob = 1 - (soft_factor * rand()) where soft_factor ~ [0, SOFT_THROTTLE_MAX]
